page: Amazon Web Services g4ad.xlarge is a graphics-focused instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor with x86_64 architecture. It features 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, running at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, a dedicated local storage volume of 150 GB NVMe SSD, and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Graphics acceleration is provided by a single AMD Radeon Pro Navi V520 GPU with 8 GB of VRAM.

Benchmark data indicates that the CPU and memory performance of this instance is generally modest. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests place the instance in the bottom 10% of performance. Similarly, memory bandwidth tests for both read and write operations fall into the bottom 25%. However, the instance achieves average performance in single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, as well as Geekbench single-core testing. For LLM inference, the instance manages average text generation speeds of 103.47 tokens per second on small 135M models, but drops to a poor 5.34 tokens per second on medium 7B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the g4ad.xlarge offers a bundled GPU and local NVMe SSD storage on the Nitro hypervisor, which provides dedicated resources without the premium cost of high-end enterprise accelerators. The primary tradeoff is the lower CPU and memory performance profile, as evidenced by weak database operations and static web serving throughput benchmarks. This makes the instance less suitable for heavy compute or high-throughput database workloads, but highly specialized for workloads that can leverage the AMD Radeon Pro GPU and local NVMe storage.
Appropriate workloads for the g4ad.xlarge include graphics-intensive applications, basic GPU-accelerated rendering, remote workstations, and light machine learning inference on small models.
